subject: general
question: Article 246A of the Constitution of India gives power to both Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Taxation of Goods and Services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 246A of the Indian Constitution was introduced through the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016**, which enabled the implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST).
 
• It grants **concurrent powers** to both the Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws with respect to GST.
 
• Under this article, the Parliament has exclusive power to make laws on **inter-state trade or commerce of goods and services**, while both Parliament and State Legislatures can legislate on intra-state transactions.
 
• GST subsumes multiple indirect taxes such as VAT, Service Tax, Excise Duty, and others, simplifying India's indirect taxation system.
 
• The introduction of Article 246A aimed to promote a unified market, enhance ease of doing business, and eliminate the cascading effects of taxes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Property Rights (Option 1):**

 
 
• Property rights in India are addressed under Article 300A of the Indian Constitution, which states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
 
• Initially, property rights were a fundamental right under Article 31, but it was abolished by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, and made a legal right under Article 300A.
 
• This provision ensures that private property cannot be taken away without due process of law or proper compensation.
 
 
 
• **Emergency Provisions (Option 3):**
 
 
• Emergency provisions are detailed under Part XVIII (Articles 352 to 360) of the Indian Constitution.
 
• These provisions enable the government to assume greater control during times of crisis and include three types of emergencies: National Emergency (Article 352), State Emergency/President’s Rule (Article 356), and Financial Emergency (Article 360).
 
• These provisions are invoked to safeguard the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India during extraordinary situations.
 
 
 
• **Criminal Law (Option 4):**
 
 
• Criminal law in India is primarily governed by the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973, and various special laws.
 
• The Parliament and state legislatures can legislate on criminal law under the Concurrent List (List III) of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution.
 
• Criminal law ensures the maintenance of public order, punishment for offenses, and the protection of citizens’ rights.
